findings.title: checkClosure still skips the verified-round ancestry check when the round's source_commit is (self-declared) absent. A present fix that is in the gate candidate but NOT in the verifying run's starting history closes a finding. D-039 now requires head_commit_at_start to be present, so the head could bind the fix instead.
findings.reproduction: QA_REPO_ROOT=<complete clone of the candidate> node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r23.test.mjs, case QA23-P1 (log docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-23/13-qa23-negative-suite.log). Start from the independent fixture, which validates with 0 errors (QA23-G0). (1) Commit a round-3 manifest whose entries hash correctly to its candidate_id and whose source_commit = 'ab' x 20 (never existed). Add a matching stages.json round-3 entry. (2) The qa-verifier round-3 run's head_commit_at_start is a PRESENT commit that contains that manifest but does not have the fix in its history (the fixture uses a parentless commit on a kept branch; on a linear history this is any fix committed after the run started). (3) The run's sidecar closes F-DG0-201 (High). The mirror sets fix_revision = a real commit that IS an ancestor of the gate candidate. validateGate = [] (ACCEPTED). Root cause: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs checkClosure `if (commitPresent(repo, round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(repo, f.fix_revision, round.source_commit))` skips the round binding when round.source_commit is absent. That is a corollary of findManifest's D-035 tolerance and is documented in D-039 ('when its source_commit resolves'). The fix is not compared with the verifying run's head_commit_at_start, which D-039 now requires to be present.
findings.expected: A CLOSED_VERIFIED fix_revision is bound to content the verifier could have seen, whatever the round metadata says. Proposal: in checkClosure, also require isAncestor(fix_revision, <verifying run's head_commit_at_start>), or use that as the fallback when round.source_commit is absent. The head is now always present and must contain the round manifest, and on a genuine history fix <= source_commit <= freeze/manifest commit <= head. Feasibility on the real history: all 104 CLOSED_VERIFIED fixes are already ancestors of their verifying run's head, and none is verified in a round whose source_commit is absent (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-23/21-fix-revision-integrity-nl.log). So the stricter rule costs nothing today. Add a unit test for the QA23-P1 shape.
findings.actual: validateGate returns 0 errors for QA23-P1. Scope is narrower than F-DG0-246, which this round verifies as fixed: the fix must be a real, present commit in the gate candidate (QA23-N1/N2/N4 show absent, all-zero and off-branch fixes are rejected), and the closure still comes from a genuine reviewer sidecar. Only the binding between the verifying run and the named fix commit depends on orchestrator-written round metadata. No real closure is affected (0 on the full history).
